title: SPT-01: executeSaga() creates tenant DB row but never calls provisionTenantSchema() — tenant schemas missing for all tenants

root_cause.summary: The onboarding saga (executeSaga in src/identity/onboarding.zig) creates a row in public.tenant and provisions Keycloak (realm, user, roles, client, hostname), but has no step that calls provisionTenantSchema() from src/db/provisioning.zig. The SagaState struct has no schema_provisioned flag, and the compensate() function has no schema drop path. As a result every successfully onboarded tenant has a public.tenant row with no corresponding public.tenant_schemas row and no physical PostgreSQL schema.

code_location.gap: Between step 1 (createTenantInDb) and step 2 (provisionRealm) there is no call to provisionTenantSchema. SagaState has no schema_provisioned field. compensate() has no schema teardown.

root_cause.why_not_caught_earlier: Integration tests for SPT-01 were not included in the test suite at the time executeSaga was authored. The function compiles and runs without error because provisionTenantSchema is never called — not called means no error propagated.

reproduction: POST /api/v1/tenants with a valid onboarding payload
HTTP 201 is returned — onboarding appears successful
SELECT schema_name FROM information_schema.schemata WHERE schema_name LIKE 'tenant_%'; — returns 0 rows
Any subsequent query that targets the tenant schema fails with 'schema does not exist'

fix_plan.description: BACKEND-DEV must implement three changes. CODE-DESIGNER will produce the design artefact for step 02.

changes.change: Add schema_provisioned: bool = false to SagaState. After createTenantInDb() succeeds and saga.tenant_created is set, call db_provisioning.provisionTenantSchema(allocator, pool, tenant.tenant_id, migrations_dir). Set saga.schema_provisioned = true on success. Map ProvisionError variants to OnboardingError (PoolExhausted, PersistenceFailed, OutOfMemory as appropriate). executeSaga must accept a migrations_dir: []const u8 parameter to pass through to provisionTenantSchema.
changes.compensation: In compensate(), if saga.schema_provisioned and saga.tenant_id != null, call a new dropTenantSchema() helper that executes: SELECT public.bpm_drop_tenant_schema($1::uuid). Add schema_provisioned: bool = false to SagaState.

changes.change: At server startup, after runMigrations() completes for the public schema, call provisionTenantSchema(allocator, pool, default_tenant_id, migrations_dir) for the all-zeros default tenant UUID. provisionTenantSchema is idempotent, so repeated calls are safe. This ensures the default tenant schema exists even if it was not provisioned during onboarding (pre-fix tenants).

Write a migration (or standalone zig build migrate step) that iterates public.tenant and calls bpm_provision_tenant_schema(tenant_id) for each tenant not already in public.tenant_schemas. This retroactively provisions schemas for all tenants created before the fix (e.g. swiftroute). Must be idempotent.
changes.note: Exact migration number to be assigned by BACKEND-DEV at implementation time

fix_plan.provisionTenantSchema_signature: provisionTenantSchema(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, pool: *Pool, tenant_id_str: []const u8, migrations_dir: []const u8) ProvisionError!void
fix_plan.import_required: const db_provisioning = @import('db/provisioning.zig'); (adjust module alias to match build.zig imports in onboarding.zig)

acceptance_criteria: After POST /api/v1/tenants, public.tenant_schemas contains exactly one row for the new tenant
A physical schema named tenant_<uuid_no_dashes> exists in bpm_dev and bpm_test
If any step after schema provisioning fails, compensate() drops the tenant schema row (bpm_drop_tenant_schema called)
provisionTenantSchema is called at server startup for the default tenant (idempotent)
All existing tenants (swiftroute, default) have schemas after zig build migrate runs the retroactive migration
zig build test-integration passes all SPT-01 tests
